Rules:
- single: 0-1 worktree stories, OR one high-effort story that needs focused attention (e.g., an investigator role verifying CheckoutForm.tsx validation logic, or an implementer writing the case-sensitivity fix for email/confirmEmail)
- parallel: 2-4 independent stories with no shared file scope
- sequential: stories with overlapping file scope, tight coupling, or shared state risk

Overlapping file scope outranks story count. Stories that edit the same file must not run in
parallel worktrees, even when there are only two or three of them: the count alone cannot see
that, and parallel worktrees over a shared file produce a merge conflict the run cannot resolve.

For the Go Transit checkout email validation fix, watch for file-scope overlap between the investigator role
(verifying CheckoutForm.tsx line numbers and validation logic) and the implementer role (fixing the case-sensitivity bug).
Both are likely to edit the same validation files, so sequential execution prevents merge conflicts.
